title: PowerPoint on desktop: attach and reference an image when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, image-reference workflow, licence-assignment path and PowerShell command are supported. Its licensing and feature-specific control gaps remain appropriately qualified, and the documented connected-experience restriction is accurately described.

claims.claim: No feature-specific administrator setting for image attachment is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint attach reference image Agent Mode admin disable image attachment policy. Read release notes and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings; image generation and general access controls do not document an image-attachment switch.

claims.claim: The feature documentation specifies no administrator action to enable image referencing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint attach reference image Agent Mode admin disable image attachment policy. Read the roadmap, release-note entry and Copilot admin settings; the feature's steps are user actions, with no feature-specific administrator enablement action.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default state is user-opt-in: users choose to attach an image when creating a presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint attach reference image Agent Mode admin disable image attachment policy; read release notes and Copilot admin settings. "Use the Copilot pane to enter a prompt and attach an image you want to use in your presentation." No attachment-specific switch found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[0].governs; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence gives users the full Copilot experience in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Users without the add-on licence can have Copilot in PowerPoint through the Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) experience.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Chat experiences in Word, Excel and PowerPoint vary with the user's licence and tenant configuration.
claims.quote: Chat experiences in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint vary depending on the user's license and tenant configuration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is included as a new option inside the existing licensed Copilot in PowerPoint experience, not a separately documented feature licence.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published which licence tier specifically includes attached-image referencing during presentation creation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference attached images presentation license Basic add-on pricing meter Agent Mode. Read release notes, Copilot overview and requirements. Basic lists creation and adding images, not this referencing feature; Copilot-app Agents are a different experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No price specific to image referencing is published in the roadmap or Microsoft documentation checked.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot attached image referencing consumption credits meter pricing. Read roadmap, release notes, Copilot overview and usage-based billing overview; no feature-specific price found.

claims.claim: No meter for this image-reference feature is documented at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot attached image referencing consumption credits meter pricing. Read release notes, Copilot overview and Understand usage-based billing and cost management for Copilot Credits. None names a meter for attaching and referencing an image in PowerPoint.

claims.claim: The documented licence-assignment control applies to user accounts.
claims.quote: You can assign or unassign licenses for users in the Microsoft 365 admin center on either the Active users page, or on the Licenses page.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is available in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page.
Select a product.
On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified licence to a user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The table's control assigns the Copilot licence rather than switching image attachment on or off separately.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyze content on organizational devices makes Copilot features unavailable in PowerPoint and the other listed apps.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
- Excel
- OneNote
- Outlook
- PowerPoint
- Word
